title: Contributor Journey and Sunrise/Sunset Procedure for Design System
creator: Maya Chen
description: This ticket codifies a repeatable contributor journey and a clear sunrise (onboarding new components/tokens) and sunset (deprecation) procedure for Redwood's design system. The goal is to reduce ad-hoc component churn, improve discoverability of migration paths, and set measurable guardrails for removal so product teams can plan migrations with confidence. Deliverables: an editable playbook page, a PR template snippet, an intake triage rubric, and a standardized deprecation timeline with stakeholder notifications.
acceptance_criteria: A single canonical playbook page exists in Design Docs with contributor journey steps and a downloadable checklist
PR template snippet is merged into the design-system repo and referenced in contribution docs
Triage rubric implemented as a lightweight Google Form + Slack workflow for initial intake
Sunrise checklist (accessibility, tokens, visual regression tests, usage docs) is defined and validated with 3 pilot components
Sunset policy implemented: deprecation announcement template, 90-day soft deprecation window, automated usage telemetry to validate removal readiness
Cross-team reviewers (Engineering, PM, Security, DX) listed and contacted in the playbook
Migration guides created for 2 high-usage components and linked from the component pages
tasks: Draft contributor journey narrative and map key decision gates
Create a single-page playbook in Design Docs and export as markdown
Add PR template snippet to design-system repo and update contributing.md
Prototype intake triage Google Form and Slack notifier (triage channel)
Run 3 pilot contributions through the new flow (button variant, sidebar table, token update)
Audit high-usage components for current migration pain points and document examples
Define deprecation timeline and draft announcement and FAQ templates
Coordinate with Eng to add a telemetry tag for components marked for deprecation
Publish playbook and announce in #design-system and company all-hands
review_checklist: Design review: component anatomy, token usage, responsive behavior
Accessibility review: keyboard focus, ARIA roles, contrast, screen-reader text
Engineering review: props/flags for migration, backward compatibility, tests
API contract review: stable props vs experimental flags documented
Performance review: render cost, bundle impact, and potential lazy-loading
Docs review: usage examples, migration guide, changelog entry
Product review: customer impact assessment and communication plan
rfc_process: For non-trivial additions/changes, open a Design RFC in the RFC board with problem statement, proposed API, and migration strategy
RFC should include visual examples, token maps, and accessibility notes
Shared RFC draft with Engineering and PM stakeholders for a 1-week review period
Collect sign-offs from at least one Eng, one PM, and one Accessibility reviewer before implementation
If RFC impacts runtime (e.g., new render path or heavy JS), route to ENG infra for performance validation
RFCs resulting in deprecation must include: rationale, timeline, telemetry plan, and rollback criteria
deprecation_policy: Stage 1 — Notice (Day 0): Publish deprecation notice in component docs and send to affected owners. Add 'deprecated: soft' flag in registry.
Stage 2 — Soft Deprecation (Day 1–90): Component remains available; migration guides and alternatives are highlighted; collection of telemetry to measure active usage
Stage 3 — Hard Deprecation Announcement (Day 60): Reminder sent to owners and broader teams with 30-day removal warning
Stage 4 — Removal (Day 90+): If telemetry shows <1% active usage or owners confirmed migration complete, remove component from the public registry and archive docs with a reference to migration guide
Emergency removals: For security or compliance issues, escalation to Security and Product required; removal may occur faster with a documented incident review
Fallback policy: If dependent product teams cannot meet the timeline, open a migration exceptions ticket with a defined, time-boxed mitigation plan
Post-removal: Maintain an archived copy of the component with a migration snippet and a small shim package where feasible to reduce breakage
notes: We intentionally separate contributor intake from full RFCs to lower friction for small changes (tokens tweaks, docs fixes)
Pilot components chosen should represent token-only changes, compositional updates, and layout-heavy components to validate checklist coverage
Telemetry work requires a small ENG task to surface component usage by route + repo (ENG-5012)
